label: Exponential growth; fleets still small
rationale: Humanoids crossed from pilot to commercial deployment in 2025: Agility Digit at GXO moved 100,000+ totes and Figure 02 completed an 11-month BMW run. But single-site fleets remain small (2–10 units typical) and Tesla abandoned its 5,000 Optimus target; the report's summary table rates the KPI 🟡.

label: Approaching, not yet achieved
rationale: San Francisco is closest with robotaxis at ~50% of licensed taxis, and Waymo reached 450,000+ weekly rides, but Uber/Lyft still dominate and including rideshare robotaxis are <5% everywhere. All deployments are geofenced L4.

label: Distant
rationale: No robot has made coffee in a random unseen home; the closest result is π₀.5 performing cleaning tasks in unseen homes, and Figure's Helix grasping novel objects. Zero-shot reliability of ~20–50% is the core blocker, with the full test likely 2027–2030.

label: Approaching
rationale: Autonomous navigation, radiation survival and valve/switch manipulation have been demonstrated, but critical disaster-zone manipulation remains teleoperated and autonomous repair decisions are not demonstrated. TEPCO has retrieved only ~0.9 g of the ~880 t of fuel debris.

label: Approaching
rationale: No humanoid has completed a verified continuous 8-hour fully autonomous shift; Figure 02 ran 10-hour shifts for 11 months at BMW but required support staff. Deployments remain limited to 1–2 repetitive tasks, need human resets, and Optimus demos are often teleoperated.

label: Progressing: Waymo ~2,500 cars/6 US cities, Baidu 1,000+ in Wuhan; no metro share data, ETA 5-10 yrs
rationale: No event shows robotaxis outnumbering human-driven taxis in any metropolitan area, and every deployment is geofenced L4, not L5. The milestone's own quantity is growing: Waymo went from 250,000 to 450,000+ paid rides per week between April and December 2025 (about 2,500 vehicles in 6 US cities), and Baidu Apollo Go runs 1,000+ vehicles in Wuhan and 250,000+ weekly rides across 22 cities. The ledger has no city-level robotaxi-versus-taxi count, so a <=5-year ETA is not evidenced; the faster timelines are proponent targets (Tesla missed all of its 2025 ones), which leaves a credible ETA of 5-10 years.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity (robotaxi fleet/rides per metro) with a credible ETA of 5-10 years; not green because no metro-level robotaxi-vs-taxi count is evidenced (no demonstrated precursor at relevant scale with non-proponent corroboration of the share)
basis.eta: 5-10 years (~2031-2036); a shorter ETA (e.g. San Francisco or Wuhan) is plausible but not evidenced by any city-level fleet-versus-taxi count in the ledger
basis.path: Waymo (US; 250k -> 450k+ paid weekly rides Apr -> Dec 2025, ~2,500 vehicles in 6 cities, freeway service) and Baidu Apollo Go (1,000+ vehicles in Wuhan, per-vehicle profitability there, 250k+ weekly rides in 22 cities); Pony.ai city-wide Shenzhen permit
blockers: Definitional: '(L5 Transport Solved)' vs. all deployments geofenced L4; whether ride-hail counts as 'human-driven taxis' changes the denominator by an order of magnitude
Data: no metro-level robotaxi vs human-driven taxi count in the ledger
Safety/regulatory: recalls and incidents (Waymo school-bus recall Dec 2025, Baidu Zhengzhou crash, Cruise shutdown 2024)
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; status stays yellow. The previous assessment (2026-01-04-milestone-robotaxi-saturation) used the non-bound label 'Approaching, not yet achieved' and gave no ETA or path. It rested on an SF '~50% of licensed taxis' figure that no ledger event supports, and it cited records since superseded by re-verified versions. Under v1 yellow rests on measured fleet/ride growth with a 5-10 year ETA; proponent timelines do not set it.

label: Achieved: Figure 02 humanoids ran 10-hour shifts Mon-Fri on BMW's Spartanburg line (2025)
rationale: Figure AI's primary report, re-verified 2026-09-30 and corroborated by Assembly Magazine, states that Figure 02 humanoids (a general-purpose robot) ran 10-hour shifts Monday-Friday for months on an active BMW assembly line. They logged 1,250+ hours of runtime, loaded 90,000+ parts and contributed to 30,000+ X3 vehicles. That meets the literal wording: a full (>=8-hour) shift, in a real factory, working alongside human associates. The wording does not require a single charge, zero interventions or the absence of support staff, so those caveats do not block 'achieved'. Agility Digit's commercial GXO deployment (100,000+ totes) is a corroborating logistics case.

basis.rule: Milestone achieved: verified (non-legacy) achievement event from a primary source (figure.ai/news/production-at-bmw) meeting the literal wording: general-purpose robot + full 8-hour shift (10-hour shifts) + real workplace (BMW Spartanburg factory) + alongside humans; no 'definitively' clause
basis.eta: achieved (2025; deployment ran ~11 months, full daily deployment from month 10 of the programme, reported Nov 2025)
basis.path: Figure 02 at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg (sheet-metal loading on an active assembly line); corroborating: Agility Digit at GXO (commercial logistics)
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; yellow -> achieved. The previous assessment (2026-01-04-milestone-the-blue-collar-shift) used the non-bound label 'Approaching'. It judged against criteria that are not in the milestone's wording: a 'continuous', 'fully autonomous' shift with no support staff. It also relied on Optimus teleoperation stories that are irrelevant to the Figure case. STATUS.md makes 'achieved' a test of the literal wording, which the verified primary Figure/BMW record (10-hour shifts on a real line alongside humans) meets.

label: Distant: autonomous site navigation only; disaster-zone manipulation still teleoperated, ETA >10 yrs
rationale: Robots do navigate real disaster and nuclear sites: Spot runs ongoing inspection deployments at Fukushima Daiichi, Chernobyl and Sellafield, and DARPA's Triage Challenge robots navigated simulated crash scenes. The repair half of the milestone has no evidenced precursor, though: all manipulation inside Fukushima Daiichi is still teleoperated, and fuel-debris retrieval stands at grams (about 0.7 g per retrieval) out of ~880 t. No funded programme in the ledger targets autonomous valve/switch repair in a disaster zone (UK NDA Auto-SAS is waste sorting, and Atlas LBM is a lab demo). No evidenced path gets there within 10 years.

basis.rule: Milestone red: ETA over 10 years / no evidenced path for the autonomous critical-repair component; only the navigation half has deployed precursors
basis.eta: >10 years (no evidenced precursor or programme for autonomous valve/switch repair in a disaster zone)
basis.path: Navigation: Spot inspection deployments at Fukushima Daiichi/Chernobyl/Sellafield, DARPA Triage Challenge (simulated crash scenes). Manipulation: Fukushima debris retrieval (teleoperated, grams), UK NDA Auto-SAS autonomous waste sorting (GBP 9.5M), Atlas LBM (lab demo, legacy record)
blockers: Technical: autonomous manipulation under radiation, debris and degraded comms is not demonstrated; the real disaster-site interventions are teleoperated
Programmatic: no funded programme in evidence targets autonomous repair in disaster zones (current programmes target inspection, sorting, triage)
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; yellow -> red. The previous assessment (2026-01-04-milestone-the-fukushima-test) used the non-bound label 'Approaching' and gave no ETA. Its yellow rested on the claim that 'valve/switch manipulation has been demonstrated', which no ledger event supports. It also admitted that critical manipulation remains teleoperated and that autonomous repair is not demonstrated. Under v1 yellow needs measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity with a credible 5-10 year ETA. The repair component has neither, so the status is red (Distant).

label: Progressing: pi0.5 does multi-step chores in unseen homes; no coffee in unseen home, ETA 5-10 yrs
rationale: No robot has made coffee in a random, previously unseen home. The milestone's own quantity is moving, though: Physical Intelligence's pi0.5 (April 2025) performed multi-step cleaning tasks in homes never seen during training, and Figure's Helix grasps novel household objects from language commands. That supports a credible ETA of 5-10 years. It is not green because that precursor is reported only by its developer, and non-proponent benchmarks (REALM, VLA open-challenge survey) find generalization and long-horizon tasks still fragile. Home-robot announcements (1X NEO pre-orders, Gemini Robotics) cannot lift the status.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity (autonomous multi-step household tasks in unseen homes) with a credible ETA of 5-10 years; not green because the precursor lacks non-proponent corroboration and independent benchmarks show fragile generalization
basis.path: Generalist VLA policies on mobile manipulators: Physical Intelligence pi0.5 (unseen-home chores; $600M Series B), Figure Helix/Figure 03 (novel-object grasping; $1B+ Series C), Google DeepMind Gemini Robotics
blockers: Technical: zero-shot reliability on long-horizon tasks (REALM: pi0/GR00T fragile under perturbation; VLA survey: compounding errors)
Technical: no evidenced operation of unfamiliar appliances or liquid handling in unseen homes
Safety: home deployment safety (Agility will not enter homes until falls are provably safe)
basis.change_note: Rubric correction v1, no new evidence; red -> yellow. The previous assessment (2026-01-04-milestone-the-wozniak-test) used the bare label 'Distant', which scored the distance to the goal. Its own stated ETA ('likely 2027-2030') is well under 10 years and contradicts red, and it cited superseded records. Under v1 red needs an evidenced ETA over 10 years or no path. The verified pi0.5 unseen-home result is measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity, with a credible 5-10 year ETA, so the status is yellow (Progressing).

rationale: STATUS.md v1 cannot judge this KPI: no KPI metric registered (single-site fleet sizes are undisclosed). The previous pre-rubric status (yellow) is withdrawn from display rather than carried.

label: Progressing: Figure 02 ran daily 10h BMW shifts; intervention & throughput rates undisclosed
rationale: Under the tightened wording, the verified Figure 02/BMW record shows full 10-hour shifts on every working day of an active line for months, alongside humans. That is real progress on the milestone's own quantity, but neither Figure nor BMW/Assembly Mag discloses the achieved interventions per shift, the throughput against the 84 s cycle requirement, or the absence of teleoperation (Figure lists only targets and 'every intervention logged'), so it does not meet the literal wording. Digit at GXO (about 4 h per battery, 100k+ totes) has the same disclosure gap. A ≤5-year path rests only on proponent claims (Figure 03 as successor) with no non-proponent corroboration of the binding metrics, so this is yellow, not green.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress on the milestone's own quantity (8h+ shifts on consecutive working days in a real factory alongside humans), with an ETA of ≤5 years asserted only by the proponent. Not achieved: no verified event discloses ≤1 intervention/shift on average, ≥90% of required throughput, or no teleoperation. Not green: no non-proponent corroboration of those metrics.
basis.eta: 5-10 years on evidence; ≤5 years only on proponent assertion (Figure 03 successor programme)
basis.path: Figure (Series C >$1B) at BMW Spartanburg: Figure 02 ran 10h shifts Mon-Fri, every working day for months (2 robots, 1,250+ h, 90k+ parts), now retired in favour of Figure 03. Secondary path: Agility Digit RaaS at GXO (100k+ totes, ~4 h battery + autonomous docking).
blockers: Disclosure gap (reporting, not structural): no deployer publishes achieved interventions/shift, throughput vs requirement, or teleoperation status; Figure gives only targets (0 interventions, 84 s cycle) and says interventions were logged
Technical: 4-6 h per charge needs swaps/docking to cover 8h+ shifts; long-horizon VLA fragility (compounding errors)
basis.change_note: Definition change 4cba345 (STATUS rule 6): achieved -> yellow. The new wording requires 30 consecutive working days of 8h+ shifts with no teleoperation, a disclosed average of ≤1 human intervention per shift and ≥90% of the job's throughput. The Figure/BMW record that was enough under the old 'one full 8-hour shift' wording gives none of the three performance disclosures, so 'achieved' no longer holds. No new evidence: the reassessment is purely the wording change.
